global_read: global.json (15:48) shows the tape has turned distinctly more cautious than yesterday's calm read. VIX jumped +11.51% 1d to 15.89 (still low vs history but the direction matters -- a real one-day fear spike, not noise). Brent is holding near $90.69 with a modest -0.2% 1d print in the feed, but real-time reporting today has Brent trading above $90-91 intraday on Strait of Hormuz shipping disruption -- a direct hit to Pakistan's energy import bill given ~90% of its oil/LNG transits Hormuz. Gold's safe-haven bid persists (+0.81% 1d, +11.05% 1mo) -- flight-to-safety flows are intensifying, not fading. S&P/Dow are only mildly softer (-0.17%/-0.20% 1d) so the US tape itself isn't panicking, but USD/PKR ticked up +0.44% 1d. Net: today's driver is a genuine geopolitical energy-security shock (US-Iran ceasefire expiry, Hormuz tanker traffic collapse), not a mechanical wobble -- it is directly relevant to PSX today, which itself fell over 1% intraday (KSE-100 down >2,000 points around midday). This argues for risk-off, not neutral.
drivers: KSE-100 fell over 2,000 points (~1%+) intraday on 2026-08-18 amid heightened Middle East tensions as the US-Iran ceasefire deadline expired without a deal; selling was broad across autos, cement, banks, E&P and OMCs/power (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40435341/psx-benchmark-index-down-over-2000-points)

The 60-day US-Iran ceasefire under the Islamabad framework expired 2026-08-17 without a lasting agreement, stuck on Strait of Hormuz freedom-of-navigation and frozen-funds issues -- talks described by a senior White House official as 'static' (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/cnbc-daily-open-us-iran-war-ceasefire-expire.html)
